column41: Please do not mark these two cats as wild. These two cats are to my knowledge NOT owned by anyone on this street, and were very wary of my movement. I first spotted the orange cat walking along the road, this cat than sprinted into a hedge of a front yard upon seeing me, before running to the other side of the yard which is seen in the photos I took. This orange cat spooked another cat that was hiding behind the hedges Both cats moved Everytime I went to adjust my camera. These photos were taken on a 300mm lens, by the time the picture was taken the cats appeared to calm down. I am familiar with the owners of this house, and have to talked to them before and they do not own any cats, their neighbour owns a white cat however these two do not match the description. I am also aware of most of the cats on this street, which also look nothing like these two. The orange cat may be related to a stray-turned wild individual of a similar colouring that lives in this section of the street, however it is unknown. Please do not mark animals captive without reason as these were very wild cats

I do not know whether CNM distinguishes between feral and domestic cats. This is the sighting of a domestic cat. I observe this red cat regularly around the same site at the Fair when I leave after a weeding session in the evening. Occasionally I saw this cat involved in a fight with another cat.  The cat was hunting a small mammal presumably a rat - rats are attracted to this area by the rotten food that people occasionally dump in the nature reserve. The Fair residential estate has been declared a cat containment right before the first residents moved in. A cat containment sign which has been put up after many complaints about roaming cats (including by The Fair residents) has been vandalised and to my knowledge, no further action was taken to implement the cat containment rules.

column77: Kosciuszko National Park - Upslope of Snow Ridge Road and south of Snow Ridge Quarry B, SE of Cabramurra
column88: Heavily burnt in 2003 wildfire, with no remaining live trees but just a sea of standing dead trees on upper SW facing slope. Regenerating eucalypts (mainly Alpine Ash and some Snow Gums) with a moderate shrub layer including several Acacia sp, Bossiaea sp, Mountain Pepper, Grevillea victoriae and Pimelea sp. Ground layer dominated by tussock grasses and Dianella tasmanica. An area of boulderfield in a slight drainage line with little vegetation except Rubus parvifolius clumps of Polystichum proliferum and lots of moss that went downslope to below road.

column88: Heavily burnt in 2003 wildfire, with no remaining live trees but just a sea of standing dead trees on upper SW facing slope. Regenerating eucalypts (mainly Alpine Ash and some Snow Gums) with a moderate shrub layer including several Acacia sp, Bossiaea sp, Mountain Pepper, Grevillea victoriae and Pimelea sp. Ground layer dominated by tussock grasses and Dianella tasmanica. An area of boulderfield in a slight drainage line with little vegetation except Rubus parvifolius clumps of Polystichum proliferum and lots of moss that went downslope to below road.
